profile.title: S-CLAY1 — Wheeler et al. (2003)
profile.summary: A soft-clay plasticity model that represents directional yielding and changes in fabric during permanent deformation.
profile.introduction: Soft clay can retain a preferred direction from its deposition and loading history. S-CLAY1 describes this plastic anisotropy with an inclined yield surface: the boundary between elastic response and further permanent deformation changes with the material’s internal fabric.
behaviours: The stress needed to reach yielding depends on the loading direction relative to the clay’s fabric. A tilted yield surface distinguishes this response from an isotropic clay idealization.
Plastic volumetric and shear deformation change the fabric and therefore the inclination of the yield surface. The hardening law assigns different target directions to these two contributions.
Plastic volumetric deformation also changes the size of the yield surface. This size change is distinct from its rotation.
profile.parameterNote: The original paper is needed for a complete, consistent material parameter set and its calibration conventions. No laboratory preset is supplied for this entry.
profile.preparation: Stress, volume, yield-surface size and initial fabric must describe the same prepared material. The presentation illustrates an initially cross-anisotropic fabric aligned with the vertical axis; it does not supply a complete general starting-state procedure.
profile.scope: This reading profile identifies the original2003 S-CLAY1 formulation for soft clay using effective stress. A public laboratory run is unavailable for this entry.
profile.limits: The original S-CLAY1 formulation and S-CLAY1S are different: S-CLAY1S adds bonding and its degradation. Creep extensions and altered yield surfaces also require their own definitions. A Modified Cam Clay parameter set cannot supply missing fabric parameters or initial conditions.
